$comment: THE ONE PLACE THAT SAYS WHICH BACKEND IS ACTUALLY SERVING TRAFFIC.
This file exists because five files disagreed and nothing noticed. As of
2026-08-14 the repository contained: fly.toml declaring an app in Mumbai,
a Dockerfile built for it, keep-warm.yml pinging Render with a comment
explaining that it had spent a week pinging a Fly host that does not
resolve, a frontend CSP allowing BOTH origins, and no Render configuration
at all — the live host's settings lived only in a dashboard.
The cost of that was measured, twice, and is written up in
.github/workflows/keep-warm.yml: the warmer reported itself healthy while
pinging nothing, and real arrivals paid a 22.5-second cold boot.
backend/lib/deployment-config.test.js reads this file and fails when any
of those artefacts drifts from it. Editing this file is how a cutover
happens; editing one artefact alone is now a red test rather than a
NOTHING SECRET LIVES HERE. Hostnames and regions only — the repository is
public. Keys stay in the host's own environment.

live.$comment: The host that answers today. Change this LAST in a cutover, once the new host is already serving.

prepared.$comment: Built and committed, never deployed: Fly wants payment. docs/MUMBAI-MIGRATION.md has the plan and scripts/verify-migration.sh the check. `alop-ai-backend.fly.dev` does NOT resolve — do not point anything at it until it does.

runtime.$comment: One Node major across the Dockerfile, CI, render.yaml and package.json engines. deployment-config.test.js already pinned the first three to each other; this is the number they are pinned TO.
